newsitem.title: USA: A silent Christmas Eve for U.S. mortgage-backeds.
newsitem.headline: A silent Christmas Eve for U.S. mortgage-backeds.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backeds were broadly flat as numerous market players abandoned their trading posts early for the Christmas holiday while some refused to show up at all, traders said.
Since PSA The Bond Market Trade Association recommended the U.S. bond markets close at 1400 EST/1900 GMT on Tuesday and all day Wednesday, many market players decided to play hookey, they said.
"Nothing is going on," said one New York-based trader. He said about half of his colleagues failed to report to work.
"(Trading today) is a waste of computer time," he added.
A dearth of economic data Tuesday is also responsible for the lack of trading activity in the market, another mortgage trader said.
"It's completely dead ... we're just sitting on our hands until we get some indication of where the economy is heading," he said.
By midday Tuesday, pass-throughs were flat across the board.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 7.0 percent coupons were on par with yesterday's close at 100-13/32, yielding 113 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac paper was flat as well, at 100-09/32 and 100-13/32, respectively.
The 10-year Treasury note was up 1/32 to yield 6.34 percent.
Trading in U.S. bond markets will resume on Thursday.
